review.item: Official game log in the repo stops at Week 8.
review.detail: origination/data/games-2026-w1-w8.json has 121 games, max week 8. nfl.com standings (S1) show 30 teams with exactly one game since Week 8, and NYG and WAS with two. This matches Week 9 (15 games, PIT and TEN on bye) plus the Week 10 Thursday game. The repo's team records are therefore out of date.

review.item: Week 9 'fair lines' price games that are already final.
review.detail: origination/results/w9-lines.json has 15 Week 9 lines. The JAX at BAL game is Final, JAX 33 - BAL 10 (S3), but the repo has no grading of the lines. The lines are no longer forecasts and cannot be scored until a pre-game timestamp is recorded.

review.item: Third-party sportsbook prices are committed in the repo.
review.detail: data/market-lines.json holds Week 9 spreads attributed to a third-party aggregator and to FanDuel. The file's own warning says it is NOT an official source. The repo's README says no market data is used. The file is excluded from the Pages build, but it is still tracked in Git.

review.item: Python bytecode is tracked in Git.
review.detail: Two .pyc files under origination/scripts/__pycache__/ are tracked, even though .gitignore lists __pycache__/. Confirmed with git ls-files.

review.item: Several parallel websites and copies of the same data.
review.detail: The repo holds a root site (index.html, pages/), docs/, desk/, strict/, origination/, evidence-lab/, audit/, verification/, and archive/ (142 tracked files). Each has its own claims and status pages. Nothing in the repo points to one canonical site.

review.item: Duplicate session row on the coordination board.
review.detail: COORDINATION.md lists session 95e9626f twice in the Sessions table, once as 'active (integration)' and once as 'merged to main (PR #5)'.

review.item: Date heading does not match the weekday.
review.detail: origination records the nfl.com heading 'Sunday Night Football, September 9th' for NE at SEA. 2026-09-09 is a Wednesday (checked with Python's calendar). The heading was recorded by the earlier session and was NOT re-fetched here.

review.item: No depth-chart or backup data exists anywhere in the repo.
review.detail: A repo-wide search (outside archive/) finds 'depth chart' only in COORDINATION.md. The team roster page (S4) shows status only, not depth order. The second- and third-string replacement analysis the project needs has no data source yet.

review.item: Injury coverage is limited to two Week 9 games.
review.detail: data/injuries-2026-week9-candidates.json covers only CIN at ATL and NYG at PHI, and it is dated 2026-11-04. There is no Week 10 file in the repo before this session's hub/data/injuries-w10.csv.

review.item: Team abbreviation for the Rams differs between sources.
review.detail: nfl.com standings use LA. origination's game log uses LAR (recorded from the scores text). The two must be mapped before any join.

questions.question: Is betting on NFL games lawful for the user in Singapore?
questions.answer: Singapore MHA says all gambling is prohibited unless licensed, class-licensed or exempted; Singapore Pools is the only operator licensed to provide remote gambling services in Singapore.
questions.needed: A personal legal opinion from a Singapore-qualified adviser. This hub does not give one.

questions.question: How much history is needed to validate a strategy?
questions.answer: The gates in origination require at least 80 games for single-bet strategies. The repo has 121 games from 2026 only, and no earlier seasons.
questions.needed: Official game logs for earlier seasons, plus a fixed out-of-sample test window.
questions.where: nfl.com scores pages by season (not captured)

questions.question: What counts as 'winning' on the leaderboard?
questions.answer: The origination gates use loss-reduction tests. A paper-points reward system is proposed but not defined.
questions.needed: Your decision on the scoring metric (see Suggestions).

suggestions.title: Refresh official data to the current week
suggestions.why: The repo stops at Week 8 while the official standings show Week 9 and part of Week 10 are final.
options: A. Capture Weeks 9-10 scores from nfl.com and extend the game log.
B. Freeze at Week 8 and label every output as stale.
C. Start a fresh season file and keep 2026 Weeks 1-8 as a historical snapshot.
suggestions.needs: Official score pages for Weeks 9-10 (nfl.com/scores/2026/week-9 and week-10).

suggestions.title: Handle the Week 9 lines that are already final
suggestions.why: The 15 Week 9 fair lines price games that have been played (R-02).
options: A. Retire them and label them as history.
B. Grade them against official final scores, reporting the result but not as a forecast.
C. Re-originate Week 10 lines with a recorded pre-game timestamp.
suggestions.needs: Your choice. Option C requires a timestamp source.

suggestions.title: Build a depth-chart and backup tracker
suggestions.why: Needed to find which 2nd- or 3rd-string players replace starters (R-08, Q-05).
options: A. Locate an official NFL depth-chart page and verify its structure first.
B. Use official game-day inactive lists only (narrower, but official).
C. Use injury designations only (already partly captured).
suggestions.needs: Verification that an official depth-chart source exists and is stable.

suggestions.title: Complete the Week 10 injury transcription
suggestions.why: Only four full game blocks and one partial block are transcribed (Q-04).
options: A. Transcribe chunks 2-7 now.
B. Keep the partial scope and refresh on each game day.
suggestions.needs: Your choice. Option A adds about six more page chunks to transcribe.

suggestions.title: Choose one canonical website
suggestions.why: At least nine parallel sites exist (R-05, Q-13).
options: A. Make this hub canonical and archive the rest.
B. Keep all sites and link them from one index.
C. Keep the root site and retire the others.

suggestions.title: Handle the tracked sportsbook file and bytecode
suggestions.why: Unverified third-party prices and compiled Python files are in Git (R-03, R-04).
options: A. Move data/market-lines.json to archive/ and untrack the .pyc files.
B. Delete both.
C. Leave both, flagged.
suggestions.needs: Your decision. No history rewrite is proposed.

suggestions.title: Pre-register the leaderboard scoring rule
suggestions.why: Needed before any new results are scored, so a rule cannot be chosen after the outcome is known.
options: A. Paper points on Brier score.
B. Paper points on absolute error.
C. Paper ROI in units, only if licensed prices are approved (Q-08).
suggestions.needs: Your choice of metric and reward structure. No rewards are awarded by this hub.

suggestions.title: Extend the history for validation
suggestions.why: Current gates need more games and out-of-sample seasons (Q-10).
options: A. Add the 2025 season.
suggestions.needs: Your choice of range. Each season requires official score pages.

suggestions.title: Map injury designations to a weighting scheme
suggestions.why: Needed before injury status can change a line.
options: A. Display only, no weights.
B. Weights fitted on history (needs SG-08).
C. Expert-set priors, flagged as subjective.
suggestions.needs: Your choice. Option B depends on SG-08.

suggestions.title: Decide how the Singapore legal position limits the project
suggestions.why: Affects whether any wagering-related output is shown (Q-08, Q-09).
options: A. Research only, no wagering output.
B. Research output plus a note that only licensed local operators apply.
C. Get a personal legal opinion before any further work.
suggestions.needs: Your decision and, for C, your own adviser.
